checks.do: Whether the application is inside or outside China, since the connection flow differs: an in-China App Connector connects to the in-China Private Service Edge, while one outside China connects back through the premium circuit.

what-it-is.statement: Zscaler's China Premium Service for Private Access provides a way for users residing in mainland China to access private applications both inside and outside mainland China. It uses a Private Service Edge for Private Access hosted at a partner site within China, which uses a premium Chinese internet service provider (ISP) with access to both the domestic private applications in China and premium access to international private applications, and it allows traffic to be broken and inspected in China and the partner premium fabric to be used for any destination (domestic or international).

quotes: Zscaler's China Premium Service for Private Access (ZPA) feature provides a way for users residing in mainland China to access private applications both inside and outside of mainland China.
The China Premium service for Private Access uses a Private Service Edge for Private Access (ZPA) hosted at a partner site within China.

The Private Service Edge uses a premium Chinese internet service provider (ISP) with access to both the domestic private applications in China and premium access to international private applications.
This service allows you to break and inspect traffic in China, and use the partner premium fabric for any destination (domestic or international).

premium-data-centers.statement: The page lists as key benefits reliable access with multiple ISPs, resulting in improved peering among ISPs in premium data centers (Beijing and Shanghai), multi-region dual premium data centers where traffic goes based on the user's proximity to the data centers, and data redundancy in the event that a premium data center is unreachable.

quotes: Reliable access with multiple ISPs resulting in improved peering among ISPs in premium data centers (i.e., Beijing and Shanghai).
Multi-region dual premium data centers where traffic goes based on the user's proximity to the data centers.
Data redundancy in the event that a premium data center is unreachable.

apps-outside-china.statement: For private applications outside China, the user does not connect to the public data center; the user connects to the closest Private Service Edge, based on the user's location (either the Beijing or Shanghai Premium data centers), creating a Z-Tunnel which forms the M-Tunnel, and the App Connector outside China connects through the premium circuit back to the Private Service Edge, creating a Z-Tunnel which forms the M-Tunnel. The page says the Great Firewall of China doesn't block it as it is a private application.

evidence.after: Accessing private applications outside of China
quotes: The user doesn't connect to the public data center.

The user connects to the closest Private Service Edge, based on the user's location (either the Beijing or Shanghai Premium data centers), creating a Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) which forms the Microtunnel (M-Tunnel).
The App Connector outside of China connects through this premium circuit back to the Private Service Edge, creating a Z-Tunnel which forms the M-Tunnel.
The Great Firewall of China doesn't block it as it is a private application.

apps-inside-china.statement: For private applications inside China, the App Connector in China connects to the Private Service Edge in China, creating a Z-Tunnel which forms the M-Tunnel; the page says the Great Firewall of China doesn't apply in this use case, as the traffic is inside China and never crosses the China borders.

quotes: The App Connector in China then connects to the Private Service Edge in China, creating a Z-Tunnel which forms the M-Tunnel.
The Great Firewall of China doesn't apply in this use case, as the traffic is inside China and never crosses the China borders.

single-contact-and-health360.statement: Zscaler is the single point of contact for Private Access China Premium services, and the bandwidth utilization for premium services can be viewed on Health360.

evidence.after: Accessing private applications outside of China
quotes: Zscaler is the single point of contact for Private Access China Premium services.
You can view the bandwidth utilization for premium services on Health360.

prerequisites-and-license.statement: The prerequisites are that Private Access should be operational in China with private applications access provided to users there, that the Private Access bandwidth is appropriately sized in megabits per second (Mbps) for the configured private applications, and that the Zscaler Private Access Firewall Allowlist is consulted for the correct protocols, ports, domains and IP addresses. The feature is only available with a license, which allows Private Access users from China to be connected to a Private Service Edge with the Premium Circuit.

quotes: Private Access should be operational in China with private applications access provided to users in China.
Ensure your Private Access bandwidth is appropriately sized based on megabits per second (Mbps) for the configured private applications.
Refer to the Zscaler Private Access Firewall Allowlist to ensure you are using the correct IP address protocols, ports, domains, and IP addresses.
This feature is only available with a license.
The license allows Private Access users from China to be connected to Private Service Edge with the Premium Circuit.

licensing-and-bandwidth.title: Licensing and bandwidth accounting for China Premium Service for Private Access
licensing-and-bandwidth.detail: The Managing Private Access Use in China page states that a license is needed but not how licensing or bandwidth is accounted for (the captured fair-use page is for the Internet & SaaS China Premium service), whether backup bandwidth rules apply, or which Health360 view shows Private Access premium bandwidth.
